title: CoinSwitch cost model artifact, schema version 1
description: Written by notebooks/train_cost_model.ipynb (Colab) and read by app/lib/costModel.ts. Every inference rule is stated here so both sides compute the same numbers; `npm run validate:model` re-runs selfTestVectors and featureTestVectors through the TypeScript path and fails on any disagreement. Signs: positive impact and positive drift both mean the trader gets less. 'Pair' is always 'INPUT/OUTPUT' with token symbols, e.g. 'BONK/USDC'. PAIR RESOLUTION, used by every predictor: the source pair is the pair itself if it is in `pairs`; else its reverse if that is in `pairs` (reversed = true); else none. depth(pair) = 'thin' if either symbol is JUP, BONK or WIF, else 'deep'. A reversed source uses the reverse pair's parameters, its shortHorizon quantiles are negated (q'[k] = -q[100 - k]), and every coverage it touches is at least 'fallback'. With no source pair, predictors use depth-level parameters ('fallback').

modelVersion.description: Unique per training run, e.g. cost-20261017T0930Z-ab12cd34.

producer.description: What made this file: 'colab:notebooks/train_cost_model.ipynb' for the real model, or 'ts-reference-fit (example only)' for the committed example.

split.description: Time-based, never random. Rows sampled before `cutoff` train; rows at or after it test. Drift rows are split by their origin's sampledAt.

pairs.description: Every sampled pair and its depth class. Thin = involves JUP, BONK or WIF.

baselineRung.description: measuredImpactBps is relative to this rung (~$25) of the same ladder.

impactFloorBps.description: Power-law fits use only rows with measuredImpactBps above this (logs of non-positive values do not exist). Metrics use every row.

maxLadderSpanSeconds.description: Ladders whose rungs span more than this are excluded from impact fits and metrics.

measuredHorizons.description: [5, 15, 30, 60]. A drift row belongs to horizon h when |actualElapsedMs - 1000h| <= max(2000, 250h); otherwise it is excluded.

minCellN.description: A shortHorizon cell is only written with at least this many observations.

minConfidentN.description: Below this, a prediction's coverage is 'sparse'.

volatility.description: Realised volatility at time t for a pair: take that pair's rung-1 rows with t - windowMinutes*60000 <= sampledAt <= t, in time order. For each consecutive pair of rows with 0 < dt <= maxGapSeconds*1000 ms and both prices > 0, r = ln(p_i / p_{i-1}) / sqrt(dt / 60000). If fewer than minReturns such r, volatility is null. Otherwise it is the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of r, times 10000. Identical to realisedVolatility in app/lib/fillModel.ts.

features.description: The drift model's features, in order, with train-set normalisation. Each feature is z = (x - mean) / std, or 0 when std is 0. x1 = sqrt(T), x2 = vol * sqrt(T / 60), x3 = isThin * sqrt(T), with T in seconds and vol in bps/sqrt(min).

impact.description: impactBps(pair, N): params = perPair[pair], else byDepth[depth(pair)] (coverage 'fallback'). If N <= baselineNotionalUsd the result is 0. Otherwise, with params.segments present, the segment used is the last one whose fromUsd <= N and the result is segment.a * (N / 1000) ^ segment.b, floored at 0; without segments it is a * (N / 1000) ^ b, floored at 0. Coverage: no params -> 'none'; fallback -> 'fallback'; N outside [notionalMinUsd, notionalMaxUsd], the notional range of ALL the pair's training rows (not only those above the floor) -> 'extrapolated'; n < minConfidentN, where n is the segment's when segments are used -> 'sparse'; else 'ok', checked in that order. A pair not sampled in either direction uses byDepth.

cells.description: Observation counts per pair and rung, for coverage reporting.

drift.description: driftAdverseBps(pair, T, vol) = max(0, intercept + sum(coef_i * z_i)) using `features`. Target: expected adverse drift E[max(0, D_T)] in bps. When vol is null it is replaced by volFallbackByPair[source pair], else volFallbackByDepth[depth] (coverage 'fallback'). Coverage: T > max(measuredHorizons) -> 'extrapolated'; fallback -> 'fallback'; cell (source pair, nearest measured horizon) n < minConfidentN or missing -> 'sparse'; else 'ok'.

shortHorizon.description: Empirical distributions of signed drift D (bps, positive = adverse) for failure probabilities. h = the measured horizon nearest T (T beyond the largest -> largest, coverage 'extrapolated'). Lookup: '<source>|<h>|<low|mid|high>' when vol and volTertiles[source] exist, then '<source>|<h>|all', then '<depth>|<h>|all' (coverage 'fallback'). volBucket: vol < t1 low, < t2 mid, else high. failureProbability(cap) = exceedance(q, cap): 1 if cap < q[0]; 0 if cap >= q[100]; else k = max{j in 0..99 : q[j] <= cap}, u = (k + (cap - q[k]) / (q[k+1] - q[k])) / 100 when q[k+1] > q[k] else (k + 1) / 100, and P = 1 - u. Coverage: fallback -> 'fallback'; n < minConfidentN -> 'sparse'; no cell -> 'none' (P null).

metrics.description: Every metric is an object carrying its own sample count n (rule 3a). Keyed by target, then model, then depth class.

reports.description: Tables for the write-up, as arrays of row objects. Must include driftCoverage (3b), impactTable (3d) and directionalTest (3e); calibration is optional. Each row should carry an n.

selfTestVectors.description: Inputs and the notebook's own outputs. validate:model recomputes each in TypeScript; numbers must agree within |a - b| <= 1e-6 + 1e-9 * |b|, and coverage strings exactly.

featureTestVectors.description: Raw rung-1 price series and the notebook's volatility for them. validate:model recomputes each with the TypeScript feature code: the guard against train/serve skew in feature engineering, not just in the model.

powerLaw.description: impact = a (N/1000)^b, OLS in log10 space on training rows above the impact floor. Optionally a continuous piecewise power law (segments) fitted on the same rows: when present it is the prediction, and (a, b) remain the single-line fit, for comparison.

segments.description: Ascending fromUsd. segments[0].fromUsd is 0; each later fromUsd is a breakpoint, and adjacent segments agree there (relative difference under 1e-6). n is the number of fitted rows in the segment. Fitted as a continuous hinge in log10 space with the breakpoint at a rung notional, and kept only when it beats the single line on BIC.

metric.description: Any of mae, rmse, brier, value, alongside n.
